content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged Chinese pangolin frame. Host frame: the Chinese pangolin sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines an axolotl and a Chinese pangolin. Head of the Chinese pangolin, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: behavior follows head/brain donor per RC-R5-07, solitary nocturnal pangolin foraging; body is host pangolin frame and scale armor throughout; axolotl tissue only as separate surface patches, blend only at patch edges; axolotl skin in a few large patches over the back and flanks, at full strength with clean edges, color and surface unchanged inside each patch; Chinese pangolin coat everywhere else; ears are small pangolin ears, with no axolotl ear tissue; face with pangolin narrow snout and small mouth for ant/termite feeding; feet are pangolin clawed digging feet; head is pangolin head tissue including brain; limbs are short powerful pangolin legs with digging claws, support unchanged at host size; skull is pangolin skull; tail is muscular scaled pangolin tail for balance, host tissue throughout; plain coat with no stripes or spots. Coat texture flows along the body outline. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (river forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing pangolin-axolotl hybrid**
I'm planning a silhouette that uses the Chinese pangolin as the host frame with its head and scale armor, then adding distinct axolotl skin patches on the back and flanks with clean edges.
**Composing hybrid illustration**
I'm assembling a natural history illustration of the pangolin-axolotl hybrid, placing axolotl skin patches on the back and flanks against a scaled pangolin body with countershading, in a side three-quarter view on a plain light background.
**Refining axolotl patch details**
I'm preparing another generation to make the axolotl patches clearer and more natural, while keeping the soft underbelly and overall good result from the last version.
